title: Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) - Digital Database and Corresponding Interfaces for ReUse of Architectural Components (v0.6.2.0)
description:
The Catalog of Second Chances (CSC) is a prototypical digital component database. It catalogs digital representations of uniquely identifiable architectural components for reuse. Furthermore, it provides corresponding interfaces and tools to leverage them via a backend REST-API, a web-frontend as well as a interface for direct interaction within Rhino Grasshopper.

Changes in v0.6.2.0 (2026-10-18)

A robustness release (decision 8.150): the structural security items deferred by 8.144, the inline geometry budget and the follow-ups of the open-data imports. No new features.

Changed

  • Inline geometry budget (decision 8.148): a version keeps at most 1000 mesh faces and 1000 points inline. A mesh of more than 1000 faces is reduced to 1000 for the inline preview and its original goes up as detailed.ply (the rule "up to 8000 faces fully inline" is gone); every point cloud of more than 1000 points goes up in full. Applies to the shared Grasshopper library csc_gh (through CSC_Update, no component change), the robot scan processing, the geometry correction script and the open-data imports. The backend still accepts larger inline geometry; existing versions stay as they are. The tooltip of FetchReducedGeometry still says "at most 5000 points" until the next export of the components.
  • Settings (decision 8.156): the backend reads its environment in one place, src/backend/settings.py (pydantic-settings), and checks it at start: required variables, JWT_SECRET of at least 32 bytes, positive upload limits, http(s) URLs, the worker count and log level. Secrets never appear in a printed or logged settings object. Variable names and defaults are unchanged.
  • Logging (decision 8.157): the backend logs through Python's logging instead of print, into gunicorn's daily error log (API) or the dated cron logs; errors keep their traceback. No line holds user names, e-mail addresses, typed values, GitHub request URLs or the text of a rejected document.
  • Database outages answer 503 with Retry-After instead of a bare 500, and the cause goes to the log.
  • Backend modules split (decision 8.160): the snapshot routes into five modules, the identity routes into three, the Grasshopper interface routes into a package; unused 0.5 API models removed. Paths and answers are unchanged (the OpenAPI document is identical).
  • Database outages also answer 503 on the routes that handled database errors themselves; other database errors keep their answer. The client log no longer holds the text of a malformed client header, and the request line holds the path without the query string.
  • Import tools retry a request up to three times on 503 and on connection errors, honouring Retry-After; every other error stops at once.
  • One way to load a record (decision 8.158): identities, versions, evidence, datasets, invitations and materials are loaded and checked by one helper per kind, so every route answers alike. Changed answers (paths and schemas are unchanged):
  • a path id that is not a UUID answers 404 "<Kind> not found" instead of 400 "Invalid ... id"; a UUID in a body or query value stays 400;
  • "not found" texts no longer repeat the id ("Snapshot not found");
  • the file routes of a purged version answer 410 with the purge notice instead of 404;
  • a component whose current version is missing answers 409 "The component has no current state." instead of 500 (passport, compose and the exports reading through them);
  • the change log and earlier versions answer 401 to anonymous callers and 403 "Not allowed: view_history" to non-members; an outsider no longer gets a withdrawn piece's tombstone from /changes;
  • a material that does not exist answers 404 before the admin check (403 before). An unknown invitation code still answers 400, the same as a code for another address.
  • Change log (decision 8.159): evidence entries name their action (verify, attach, redact, publish, withdraw, reinstate) instead of patch; status steps stay in each record's status history. Entries carry the record's modification time and are written after it; a log entry that cannot be written no longer fails the request. Existing entries are unchanged.
  • File markers (mesh levels, point_cloud_files) are updated atomically, so uploads to the same version at once no longer lose each other's marker.
  • **CSC_Update** (decision 8.155): user objects are checked against a list of hashes from the server; unchanged files are skipped, each download is checked before it is written, and a failed file keeps the old one while the rest goes on ("Update incomplete, run again"). The result counts installed, unchanged and failed files. A replaced script component is no longer repaired automatically: it shows a remark that its inputs and outputs may have changed and that it needs a recompute.
  • FetchReducedGeometry states the inline limit correctly (at most 1000 points).

Added

  • Marker for uploaded point clouds: a snapshot lists the indices of its uploaded full point clouds in point_cloud_files (set by the upload, removed by the delete, not writable by clients), so an import resumes without probing the file.
  • Read-only mode for maintenance (decision 8.154): while the file ~/csc/shared/READ_ONLY exists, the backend answers every write with 503 and Retry-After; reads and the sign-in stay up. All workers switch at once, without a restart. The web shows a banner and disables its write buttons, /version and /health/db report read_only, and the geometry runner, the component map, the user and the geometry maintenance skip their run.

Security

  • Tokens are read with PyJWT instead of python-jose: HS256 only, exp and sub required, one verification per request. Tokens issued before the update stay valid.
  • Shared rate limits (decision 8.152): sign-in, registration, verification mails, password reset and invitations count in the database, across all workers and restarts. The read limits (lists, map, downloads, exports) count per worker; they only shed load.
  • Failed sign-ins (decision 8.162): at most 10 in 15 minutes per account, then 429 with Retry-After; an unknown account is answered the same way, and the counter holds no user name or address.
  • Request size (decision 8.163): a body over its limit is refused with 413 before it is read (uploads by their upload limit, everything else 16 MB, CSC_JSON_BODY_LIMIT_MB).
  • Usernames (decision 8.161): 3 to 32 characters, lowercase letters, digits, ., _, -, starting with a letter or digit. Every existing name already fits.
  • Release attestations (decision 8.153): every release asset carries a GitHub build attestation, and the deploy checks the backend and the frontend bundle against it before it unpacks them; it stops if the check fails or gh is missing.
  • In read-only mode the sign-in writes nothing; its per-address limit then counts in each worker's memory, and an existing account lock still holds.
  • Database connections are capped at 20 per client; a one-off dataset update no longer runs at every start.
  • Content-Security-Policy (decision 8.164): every page carries a policy built per request with a fresh nonce. Scripts run only by nonce, styles inline, everything else from the app's own origin; the exceptions are the Google map frame and images from the static host. The policy is enforced at once.

Server notes

  • JWT_ALGORITHM, if set, must be HS256; any other value stops the start.
  • The database user needs createIndex, insert, update and remove on the new collection rate_limit_counters (its TTL index is created on first use). CSC_RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE (default: the MongoDB URI) selects the store of the shared limits.
  • The read limits count per worker: the effective limit is the stated one times CSC_WORKERS.
  • The deploy installs PyJWT and removes python-jose.
  • Before the deploy, check the backend environment: FRONTEND_URL, GITHUB_REPO_URL and CSC_PUBLIC_API_URL must be http(s) URLs, the upload and photo limit variables positive, and SMTP_DEV_MODE off. The backend refuses to start otherwise and names the variable.
  • The deploy installs one new package, pydantic-settings.
  • CSC_CSP_REPORT_ONLY=1 in the frontend .env is the emergency switch for the Content-Security-Policy: the same policy is then sent as report-only (violations are logged in the browser console, nothing is blocked). Restart the frontend after setting it, and remove it once the cause is fixed.
  • Before the first deploy of 0.6.2.0, install the gh CLI binary in ~/bin and store a token for it (deployment README). The 0.6.1.1 deploy script runs first and repeats itself with the new one, which needs gh.
  • Put touch ~/csc/shared/READ_ONLY before and rm ~/csc/shared/READ_ONLY after every maintenance step (restore, purge, migration, deploy). The path is set by CSC_READ_ONLY_FLAG.
  • Deploy the server before anyone runs the new CSC_Update: it needs /ghinterface/userobject_manifest and stops with a 404 against an older server. The old CSC_Update still updates itself through the old endpoints.
  • NEXT_PUBLIC_STATIC_BASE_URL is fixed when the frontend is built (in CI): set it there, or set NEXT_STATIC_BASE_URL in the frontend environment, which is read at run time. Otherwise the policy blocks the images from the static host (the sidebar logo).

Full history: CHANGELOG.md
